Suggested: codebase-design · purpose match: codebase-design · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream gives a deep-module design vocabulary, testability rules, dependency-shaped deepening and an optional design-it-twice exercise, used when designing or changing a module interface. Our codebase-design is the same lens for the same decisions.

### Blind extraction

1. Use a fixed glossary of design terms exactly and avoid listed substitute words. (SKILL.md:10-28)
2. Treat a module's interface as everything a caller must know, including invariants, ordering, error modes, configuration and performance. (SKILL.md:16, SKILL.md:108)
3. Measure depth as leverage per unit of interface rather than as an implementation-to-interface line ratio. (SKILL.md:20, SKILL.md:107)
4. When designing an interface, ask whether methods can be fewer, parameters simpler, and more complexity hidden. (SKILL.md:54-58)
5. Depth belongs to the interface, so a deep module may contain small swappable internal parts with internal seams kept off its interface. (SKILL.md:62, DEEPENING.md:30)
6. Apply a deletion test: imagine removing the module and see whether complexity vanishes or reappears across callers. (SKILL.md:63)
7. Treat the interface as the test surface; wanting to test past it signals the wrong module shape. (SKILL.md:64, DEEPENING.md:35)
8. Introduce a seam only when at least two adapters are justified, since one adapter is mere indirection. (SKILL.md:65, DEEPENING.md:29)
9. Make code testable by accepting dependencies rather than constructing them. (SKILL.md:71-81)
10. Make code testable by returning results rather than producing side effects. (SKILL.md:83-93)
11. Keep interface surface small so fewer tests and simpler setup are needed. (SKILL.md:95)
12. Classify a deepening candidate's dependencies into in-process, local-substitutable, remote-owned, or true-external categories that dictate how it is tested. (DEEPENING.md:5-25)
13. For local-substitutable dependencies, test with the local stand-in in the suite and keep the seam internal. (DEEPENING.md:13-15)
14. For owned remote services, define a port with a production transport adapter and an in-memory test adapter. (DEEPENING.md:17-21)
15. For third-party services, inject the dependency as a port and use a mock adapter in tests. (DEEPENING.md:23-25)
16. After deepening, delete the old shallow-module unit tests once interface-level tests exist. (DEEPENING.md:34)
17. Tests assert observable outcomes through the interface and should survive internal refactors. (DEEPENING.md:36-37)
18. Before exploring alternatives, show the user a problem-space framing of constraints, dependency categories and an illustrative sketch, then proceed without waiting. (DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:9-17)
19. Spawn three or more parallel subagents that must each produce a radically different interface. (DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:21)
20. Give each design subagent a separate technical brief and a distinct constraint: minimal, flexible, common-caller-optimised, or ports-and-adapters. (DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:23-28)
21. Include both the design vocabulary and the project's domain glossary in each design brief. (DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:30)
22. Each design subagent returns interface, usage example, hidden internals, dependency strategy, and trade-offs. (DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:32-38)
23. Present designs one at a time, then compare them on depth, locality and seam placement. (DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:42)
24. Finish with an opinionated recommendation, proposing a hybrid where elements combine well. (DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:44)

Purpose: Upstream actively builds a project's glossary and ADRs while designing, used whenever domain terms or hard-to-reverse decisions come up. Our domain-modeling is the adapted copy with the same purpose and files.

### Blind extraction

1. Distinguish actively changing the domain model from merely reading the glossary, applying this discipline only to the former. (SKILL.md:8)
2. Treat a root glossary map file as the signal of a multi-context repo pointing to per-context glossaries and decision folders. (SKILL.md:24-38, GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:36-58)
3. Keep system-wide decision records at the root and context-specific ones inside each context. (SKILL.md:30-37)
4. Create glossary and decision-record files lazily, only when there is first content to write. (SKILL.md:40, ADR-FORMAT.md:5, GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:58)
5. Call out immediately when the user's term conflicts with the existing glossary. (SKILL.md:44-46)
6. Propose a precise canonical term when the user uses vague or overloaded words. (SKILL.md:48-50)
7. Invent concrete edge-case scenarios to stress-test domain relationships and concept boundaries. (SKILL.md:52-54)
8. Check user claims about behaviour against the code and surface contradictions. (SKILL.md:56-58)
9. Update the glossary inline the moment a term is resolved rather than batching. (SKILL.md:60-62)
10. Keep the glossary free of implementation detail and never use it as a spec or scratch pad. (SKILL.md:64)
11. Offer a decision record only when the decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the product of a real trade-off. (SKILL.md:66-74, ADR-FORMAT.md:29-37)
12. Name decision records with sequential zero-padded numbers and slugs, taking the highest existing number plus one. (ADR-FORMAT.md:3, ADR-FORMAT.md:25-27)
13. Use a minimal decision-record template of a title and one to three sentences of context, decision and reason. (ADR-FORMAT.md:7-15)
14. Add optional status, considered-options or consequences sections only when they add real value. (ADR-FORMAT.md:17-23)
15. Use a list of qualifying decision kinds, including architectural shape, cross-context integration, lock-in technology, scope boundaries, deliberate deviations, invisible constraints and non-obvious rejections. (ADR-FORMAT.md:39-47)
16. Use a glossary template of context name, short description, and bolded terms each with a definition and an avoid-list. (GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:3-23)
17. Pick one preferred word per concept and list synonyms under avoid. (GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:27)
18. Keep definitions to one or two sentences stating what the term is, not what it does. (GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:28)
19. Admit only project-specific terms, excluding general programming concepts. (GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:29)
20. Group terms under subheadings when natural clusters appear. (GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:30)
21. A glossary map lists each context with location and purpose plus the relationships between contexts. (GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:38-52)
22. Infer which context the current topic belongs to and ask if unclear. (GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:60)

## skill:skills/productivity/grilling

Suggested: grilling · purpose match: grilling · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream runs a relentless round-by-round interview on a plan or design when the user asks to be grilled. Our grilling is the same explicitly requested interview.

### Blind extraction

1. Interview until shared understanding, modelling decisions as a tree where each decision branches into dependent ones. (SKILL.md:6)
2. Ask in rounds containing every decision whose prerequisites are already settled. (SKILL.md:8)
3. Number each question and attach a recommended answer. (SKILL.md:8, SKILL.md:10-22)
4. Wait for the user's answers before the next round. (SKILL.md:8)
5. Format each question with a title, a body that may offer choices, and a separated recommendation. (SKILL.md:10-22)
6. Word each question so that answering yes accepts the recommendation. (SKILL.md:24)
7. Recompute the frontier after each round, deferring questions that depend on ones still open in the current round. (SKILL.md:26)
8. Look up environment facts yourself through a subagent rather than asking the user. (SKILL.md:28)
9. Do not block on fact-finding: hold back only questions downstream of the running lookup and ask the rest now. (SKILL.md:28)
10. Put every decision to the user and wait. (SKILL.md:28)
11. End only when the frontier is empty with nothing silently assumed. (SKILL.md:30)
12. Do not act on the result until the user confirms shared understanding. (SKILL.md:30)

### Mapping

- 1 → map-decisions (match)
- 2 → question-batching (match)
- 3 → recommended-answer (match)
- 4 → answer-before-next-round (new)
- 5 → round-format (match)
- 6 → yes-accepts-recommendation (match)
- 7 → question-batching (match)
- 8 → self-serve-facts (match)
- 9 → non-blocking-lookup (new)

- 12 → reconfirm-before-action (match)

- `question-batching` (new): present in `grilling`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; also in brainstorming (present), doc:AGENTS.md (variant); reason: Ours asks a batch of independent settled-prerequisite questions and defers dependent ones.
- `recommended-answer` (new): present in `grilling`; adopt, delivered; guide ok [U-09]; also in brainstorming (present); reason: Ours attaches a recommendation with its assumptions and lets the user disagree.

Purpose: Upstream breaks a spec or plan into dependency-ordered vertical-slice tickets on the tracker after the user approves the breakdown. Our planning decomposes an approved spec into Beads epics and stages with real edges.

### Blind extraction

1. Fetch and read the full body and comments of any referenced spec or issue. (SKILL.md:17)
2. Explore the codebase if needed, using glossary vocabulary and respecting decision records in ticket text. (SKILL.md:21)
3. Look for prefactoring opportunities that make the change easy, and schedule them first. (SKILL.md:23, SKILL.md:34)
4. Slice work into tracer-bullet tickets that each cut a narrow complete path through every layer. (SKILL.md:27-31)
5. Each slice must be demoable or verifiable on its own. (SKILL.md:32)
6. Size each slice to fit one fresh context window. (SKILL.md:33)
7. Give every ticket explicit blocking edges, with unblocked tickets startable immediately. (SKILL.md:38)
8. Sequence wide mechanical refactors as expand, batched migrate, then contract, each batch its own ticket blocked appropriately. (SKILL.md:40)
9. Size migrate batches by blast radius and keep CI green between batches. (SKILL.md:40)
10. When batches cannot stay green alone, share an integration branch gated by a final integrate-and-verify ticket. (SKILL.md:40)
11. Present the breakdown as a numbered list of title, blockers and delivered behaviour. (SKILL.md:44-48)
12. Ask the user about granularity, correctness of blocking edges, and merges or splits. (SKILL.md:50-54)
13. Iterate until the user approves the breakdown before publishing. (SKILL.md:56)
14. For a local tracker, write one numbered file per ticket in dependency order, never a combined file. (SKILL.md:62)
15. For a real tracker, publish in dependency order so edges reference real ids, using native blocking links where available. (SKILL.md:63)
16. Make each ticket a sub-issue when the source was an existing issue. (SKILL.md:63)
17. Label published tickets ready for an agent unless told otherwise. (SKILL.md:63)
18. Work the frontier of tickets whose blockers are all done. (SKILL.md:65)
19. Never close or modify the parent issue. (SKILL.md:67)
20. Use a local ticket template of title, end-to-end what-to-build, blocked-by, status, and acceptance checkboxes. (SKILL.md:69-82)
21. Use an issue template of parent, what-to-build, acceptance criteria and blocked-by, omitting blocked-by when native edges are set. (SKILL.md:84-103)
22. Describe what to build as user-facing end-to-end behaviour rather than a layer list. (SKILL.md:73, SKILL.md:92)
23. Avoid file paths and code snippets in tickets except trimmed decision-encoding prototype snippets noted as such. (SKILL.md:105)

## skill:skills/engineering/wayfinder

Suggested: wayfinder · purpose match: wayfinder · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream charts a large effort with unsettled decisions as a map of decision tickets on the tracker and resolves them across sessions. Our wayfinder is the Beads-native copy for the same multi-session decision mapping.

### Blind extraction

1. Name the effort's destination first, since it fixes scope. (SKILL.md:9, SKILL.md:111)
2. Produce decisions rather than deliverables by default, treating the urge to build as the signal to hand off, unless the map's notes override. (SKILL.md:11-13)
3. Refer to maps and tickets by title in human-facing text, with links inside names, never bare ids. (SKILL.md:15-17)
4. Keep the map as a single labelled tracker issue whose tickets are its child issues. (SKILL.md:21)
5. Make the map an index that gists and links each decision, which lives only in its ticket. (SKILL.md:23)
6. Default to a local-markdown tracker when none is configured. (SKILL.md:25)
7. Use a map body of destination, notes, decisions so far, not yet specified, and out of scope, without listing open tickets. (SKILL.md:27-53)
8. Write each ticket body as a single question sized to one 100K-token session. (SKILL.md:57-63)
9. Label each ticket with one type of research, prototype, grilling or task, and never with triage labels. (SKILL.md:65)
10. Claim a ticket by assigning it before any work so concurrent sessions skip it. (SKILL.md:67, SKILL.md:123)
11. Use the tracker's native blocking so the frontier is visible, falling back to a body convention only without it. (SKILL.md:69)
12. Define the frontier as open, unblocked, unclaimed children. (SKILL.md:69)
13. Record answers on resolution, not in the body, and link assets rather than pasting. (SKILL.md:71)
14. Mark each ticket as human-in-the-loop or agent-alone, and never let the agent answer the human's side of a live ticket. (SKILL.md:75)
15. Resolve research tickets with a research subagent when outside knowledge is needed. (SKILL.md:77)
16. Resolve prototype tickets by building a rough artifact and linking it as an asset. (SKILL.md:78)
17. Make grilling the default ticket type, run with the interview and domain-model skills. (SKILL.md:79)
18. Use task tickets only for manual work that unblocks a decision, driving it alone where possible or handing a checklist, and recording resulting facts. (SKILL.md:80)
19. Leave not-yet-sharp questions in a fog section rather than ticketing them, graduating them as the frontier advances. (SKILL.md:84-86)
20. Ticket a question when it can be stated precisely now, even if blocked; otherwise keep it as fog without pre-slicing. (SKILL.md:88-91)
21. Keep decided, ticketed and out-of-scope items out of the fog section. (SKILL.md:93)
22. Close tickets found beyond the destination and log them in an out-of-scope section, not in decisions so far. (SKILL.md:97-101)
23. Treat out-of-scope work as never graduating, returning only as a fresh effort if the destination changes. (SKILL.md:99)
24. Resolve at most one ticket per session, except research tickets. (SKILL.md:105)
25. When charting, grill breadth-first across the space to surface open decisions and first steps. (SKILL.md:112)
26. If charting reveals no fog, skip the map and ask the user how to proceed. (SKILL.md:112)
27. Create the map with destination and notes filled, empty decisions, and sketched fog. (SKILL.md:113)
28. Create specifiable tickets first, then wire blocking edges and cross-references in a second pass using real ids. (SKILL.md:114)
29. Fire parallel research subagents for new research tickets, storing findings on a pushed, never-merged throwaway branch pointed to from the ticket. (SKILL.md:115)
30. End the charting session without resolving any ticket. (SKILL.md:116)
31. When working the map, load only its low-resolution body. (SKILL.md:122)
32. Take the user's named ticket or else the first frontier ticket. (SKILL.md:120, SKILL.md:123)
33. Resolve by the ticket's type label, zooming into related tickets on demand and loading skills named in notes. (SKILL.md:124)
34. Record a resolution as an answer comment, close the ticket, and append a pointer to decisions so far. (SKILL.md:125)
35. After resolving, add new tickets, graduate fog, rule out-of-scope tickets out, and update or delete invalidated tickets. (SKILL.md:126)

Purpose: Upstream tdd is the reference for test-first red-green work: what a good test is, where seams go, mocking rules and loop rules, used when building or fixing test-first. Our test-driven-development fires for the same work and produces the same tests.

### Blind extraction

1. Consult the testing rules before and during every red-green cycle, not after. (SKILL.md:8)
2. Match test names and interface vocabulary to the domain glossary and respect local decision records. (SKILL.md:10)
3. Test behaviour through public interfaces so tests read like specifications and survive refactors. (SKILL.md:14, tests.md:5-23)
4. Write tests only at seams listed and confirmed with the user before any test is written. (SKILL.md:22)
5. Annotate each proposed seam with one line on what it catches and what it misses. (SKILL.md:24)
6. Consult the module-design vocabulary when the interface shape itself is in question, as a reference rather than a session. (SKILL.md:26)
7. Reject implementation-coupled tests that mock internals, test private methods, or verify through a side channel. (SKILL.md:30, tests.md:38-45)
8. Reject tautological tests whose expected value is recomputed like the code; take expected values from an independent source such as a known literal or the spec. (SKILL.md:31, tests.md:63-76)
9. Work in vertical tracer-bullet slices of one test then one implementation, never all tests first. (SKILL.md:32, SKILL.md:37)
10. Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass, with no anticipated features. (SKILL.md:36)
11. Keep refactoring out of the red-green loop and leave it to review. (SKILL.md:38)
12. Keep one logical assertion per test. (tests.md:23)
13. Avoid asserting on call counts or call order. (tests.md:42)
14. Name tests for what behaviour exists, not how it is achieved. (tests.md:22, tests.md:44)
15. Mock only at system boundaries such as external APIs, time and randomness, and sometimes databases or the filesystem. (mocking.md:3-8)
16. Never mock your own modules or internal collaborators. (mocking.md:10-14)
17. Prefer a test database over mocking the database. (mocking.md:6)
18. Inject external dependencies so they can be mocked. (mocking.md:20-35)
19. Expose external operations as specific per-operation functions rather than one generic fetcher so each mock returns one shape. (mocking.md:37-59)

### Traits

- `no-implementation-coupling` (new): present in `test-driven-development`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours avoids tests that mirror implementation and keeps internal tests only where they prove behaviour.

- `seam-preconfirmation` (new): variant via `plan-seams-no-approval`; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours deliberately takes seams from the plan without separate approval and surfaces a missing seam only when it changes scope (SKILL.md:22-24), as U-02 and O-02 reserve confirmation for material choices.

- `independent-expectation` (new): present in `test-driven-development`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours derives expected values from the spec, a worked example or a trusted fixture, never from the implementation.

Derive expected results from the spec, a worked example or another independent source.; reason: Ours runs the loop per selected behaviour (SKILL.md:28) but never forbids writing tests in bulk first; the difference is not stated as deliberate, so one clause closes it.
- `red-green` (new): present in `test-driven-development`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; also in doc:.repo-context/coding-style.md (variant), systematic-debugging (variant); reason: Ours confirms the intended failure before the fix, then implements the owning fix and reruns the check.

Owner decision: codebase-design already lists it, so this adopt completes without an edit.

- `rules-during-cycle` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours reads its test reference only when designing or changing substantive tests (SKILL.md:17-18); a mandatory read on every cycle is the chain of mandatory reads the writing principles (Routing and load) and S-04 avoid.
- `domain-vocabulary` (new): absent; reject; also in codebase-design (variant), i-have-adhd (present); reason: ROUTED: AGENTS.md:93-94 routes domain terminology and ADRs, and AGENTS.md:26 surfaces conflicts with recorded decisions; no per-skill copy.
- `respect-area-adrs` (new): absent; reject; also in doc:AGENTS.md (variant), improve-codebase-architecture (present); reason: ROUTED: AGENTS.md:93-94 routes domain terminology and ADRs, and AGENTS.md:26 surfaces conflicts with recorded decisions; no per-skill copy.
- `module-vocabulary` (new): absent; adopt, pending → codebase-design; guide ok; also in codebase-design (present); reason: HELD: codebase-design: its trigger fires on testability decisions (codebase-design/SKILL.md:3), which a test-first change makes.
- `one-assertion-per-test` (new): absent; reject; reason: A fixed one-assertion rule constrains a context-dependent choice (S-08) and conflicts with ours preferring focused parameter tables (writing-good-tests.md:17-18).

## skill:skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs

Compared with `systematic-debugging`; upstream tree hash `87c78ae966e591f9ceb177789cc5cc9de69277cd26679ffd36ca5300f430d513`.

Suggested: systematic-debugging · purpose match: systematic-debugging · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream diagnosing-bugs runs a phased diagnosis (feedback loop, reproduce, hypothesise, instrument, fix with a regression test, clean up) when a bug's cause is unclear. Our systematic-debugging covers the same trigger and produces the same confirmed cause and proving check.

### Blind extraction

1. Skip phases of the diagnosis only with explicit justification. (SKILL.md:8)
2. Read the domain glossary and nearby architecture decision records when exploring the code. (SKILL.md:10)
3. Redact every secret as a placeholder in shown commands, outputs and artifacts. (SKILL.md:14)
4. Build reproduction loops on environment variables so credentials stay out of shown text. (SKILL.md:14)
5. Quote only signal-carrying lines from captured artifacts that may hold auth headers. (SKILL.md:14)
6. Ask the user when redacted output is insufficient to diagnose. (SKILL.md:16)
7. Build a tight pass/fail feedback loop for the specific bug before anything else, investing disproportionate effort in it. (SKILL.md:18-22)
8. Try an ordered ladder of loop types from failing test through HTTP script, CLI snapshot diff, headless browser, trace replay, throwaway harness, fuzzing, bisection, differential runs, to a human-driven script last. (SKILL.md:24-35)
9. Tighten the loop for speed, symptom-specific assertions, and determinism. (SKILL.md:39-47)
10. For non-deterministic bugs, raise the reproduction rate through repetition, parallelism, stress and timing injection until debuggable. (SKILL.md:49-51)
11. When no loop can be built, stop, list what was tried, and ask for environment access, a redacted artifact, or permission for temporary production instrumentation. (SKILL.md:53-55)
12. Gate phase 1 on one already-run command shown with output that is red-capable on the user's exact symptom, deterministic, fast, and agent-runnable. (SKILL.md:57-64)
13. Stop if reading code to form a theory before the red-capable command exists. (SKILL.md:66)
14. Confirm the loop reproduces the user's described failure rather than a nearby one, repeatably, and capture the exact symptom. (SKILL.md:72-76)
15. Minimise the repro by cutting one element at a time and re-running until every remaining element is load-bearing. (SKILL.md:78-86)
16. Generate three to five ranked hypotheses before testing any. (SKILL.md:90)
17. Each hypothesis must state a falsifiable prediction in an if-cause-then-change form, or be discarded. (SKILL.md:92-96)
18. Show the ranked hypotheses to the user before testing, without blocking if they are away. (SKILL.md:98)
19. Each probe maps to one prediction and changes one variable at a time. (SKILL.md:102)
20. Prefer a debugger or REPL, then targeted logs at distinguishing boundaries, never blanket logging. (SKILL.md:104-108)
21. Tag every debug log with a unique prefix so cleanup is one search. (SKILL.md:110)
22. For performance regressions, establish a baseline measurement and bisect instead of logging. (SKILL.md:112)
23. Write the regression test before the fix only at a seam that exercises the real bug pattern. (SKILL.md:116-118)
24. When no correct seam exists, record that as an architectural finding. (SKILL.md:120)
25. If a red was forced by mutating code or a fixture, diff against a pristine copy to prove the mutation landed. (SKILL.md:125)
26. Sequence the fix as failing test, watch fail, fix, watch pass, then re-run the original unminimised loop. (SKILL.md:124-128)
27. Before declaring done, check the original repro is gone, the regression test passes or missing seam is documented, tagged instrumentation is removed, and throwaway prototypes are deleted or quarantined. (SKILL.md:132-137)
28. State the confirmed hypothesis in the commit or PR message. (SKILL.md:138)
29. A human-in-the-loop script template drives a person through step prompts and captures answers into variables. (scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh:9-30)
30. The human-loop script prints captured values as key=value lines for the agent to parse. (scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh:13, scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh:42-44)
31. Capture only observations through the human-loop script and leave sign-in to the person as a plain step, since captured values are echoed. (scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh:15-16)

### Traits

- `reproduction-first` (new): present in `systematic-debugging`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; also in doc:AGENTS.md (variant); reason: Ours reuses or builds the smallest reproduction and confirms it shows the reported failure, not a nearby one.
- `tighten-loop` (new): variant via `flake-reproduction`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; modification: Ours raises the reproduction rate for flaky failures but deliberately invests in a loop only as far as it distinguishes live causes, not as a product to keep polishing.; reason: Same purpose, looser: flake-rate raising is in non-reproducible-bugs.md:30-35, and SKILL.md:17 bounds minimisation effort to what discriminates causes.
- `reproduce-and-minimize` (new): variant via `minimize-to-discriminate`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; modification: Ours minimises only enough to distinguish live causes rather than until every element is load-bearing.; reason: Same mechanism, looser and deliberate (SKILL.md:17): extra shrinking past discrimination costs time without changing the diagnosis.
- `phase1-completion-criterion` (new): variant via `reproduction-first`; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours deliberately continues safe source analysis or instrumentation when no reproduction is obtainable and labels the fix unproven (SKILL.md:33-36), where upstream forbids any theory before a red-capable command exists.
- `fixed-hypothesis-count` (new): variant via `discriminating-observation`; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours chooses a discriminating observation instead of generating a fixed count (SKILL.md:19-20); a three-to-five quota is an invented numerical threshold (writing-principles, Pruning).
- `hypothesis-ranking-presentation` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours keeps no ranked hypothesis list to show (SKILL.md:19-20), and a mid-investigation showing adds a check-in on a routine step that U-02 and O-02 tell us to avoid.
- `one-variable-at-a-time` (new): variant via `localized-probing`; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: 3. Probe the suspected boundary or variable, changing one thing per probe, update the explanation, then repeat only while new evidence is produced.; reason: Ours probes the suspected boundary or variable (SKILL.md:21) but never limits a probe to one change, so a probe that moves two things cannot attribute the result; the difference is not stated as deliberate.
- `tagged-debug-logs` (new): present in `systematic-debugging`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours tags every instrumentation line with a unique prefix and finds it again with one grep.
- `baseline` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; also in performance-optimization (present); rewording: A performance regression needs a baseline measurement before the fix and a comparable one after it.; reason: Ours asks for comparable timing evidence for a performance regression (SKILL.md:38) without saying the baseline is taken before the fix; one clause makes the order checkable.
- `perf-bisection` (new): variant via `localized-probing`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; modification: Ours treats commit bisection as one localisation method and deliberately does not require a failed bisect before switching to performance-optimization.; reason: Same mechanism, looser and deliberate (SKILL.md:38-40); bisection stays available in localization.md:71-85.
- `debugger-first` (new): absent; reject; reason: An absolute tool preference fixes a context-dependent routine choice (U-01, S-08); ours deliberately instruments each boundary once and reads where the chain breaks (localization.md:31-42), which suits non-interactive agents.
- `prove-the-red` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: If you force the failure by mutating code or a fixture, diff against a pristine copy to confirm the mutation landed before trusting the red.; reason: Ours shows failure before the fix (SKILL.md:29-30) but has no guard against a forced red that never took effect; one sentence closes a real false-proof failure mode.
- `regression-check` (new): present in `systematic-debugging`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; also in doc:AGENTS.md (variant); reason: Ours turns the failure into a durable regression check, shows failure before and success after, then reruns the original scenario.
- `missing-seam-finding` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: When no seam can hold a regression check, record the missing seam as a finding.; reason: Ours makes the regression check conditional on feasibility (SKILL.md:29) and records remaining limits (SKILL.md:54), but never names an unreachable seam as an architectural finding.
- `closeout` (new): present in `systematic-debugging`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours removes temporary instrumentation and records cause, proving check and remaining limits.
- `delete-debug-prototypes` (new): variant via `preserve-reproducers`; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours deliberately preserves useful reproducers and user artifacts at cleanup (SKILL.md:53-54) instead of deleting or quarantining them.
- `hitl-loop-script` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A debugging task needs a person to perform a step repeatedly to reproduce a failure.; reason: A structured human-in-the-loop script is useful only when a person must repeat a step; ours requests the missing evidence instead (SKILL.md:35-36).
- `escalate-unreproducible` (new): variant via `unproven-without-reproduction`; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours continues safe source analysis without a reproduction, where upstream stops rather than hypothesize (systematic-debugging/SKILL.md:35-36).
- `justified-phase-skip` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours states the observable condition for skipping the extended investigation (an obvious localized error, SKILL.md:9-10); a per-skip justification adds ceremony that S-03 removes.
- `read-domain-docs-first` (new): absent; reject; reason: ROUTED: AGENTS.md:93-94 routes domain terminology and ADRs, and AGENTS.md:26 surfaces conflicts with recorded decisions; no per-skill copy.
- `signal-lines-only` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A debugging report leaks a credential quoted from a captured artifact.; reason: Ours keeps secrets out of reports (SKILL.md:51); quoting only signal-carrying lines is a finer technique worth adding only if the general rule proves insufficient.
- `ask-when-redaction-blinds` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours already requests missing evidence when it cannot diagnose (SKILL.md:35-36), and AGENTS.md:9-10 sets when to ask; a redaction-specific ask repeats both (S-05).
- `falsifiable-hypotheses` (new): variant via `hypotheses`; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: 2. - `seam-selection` (new): absent; adopt, pending → test-driven-development; guide ok; also in brainstorming (variant), doc:.repo-context/coding-style.md (variant), test-driven-development (present); reason: HELD: test-driven-development (.claude/skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md:20-24): Choosing the test boundary is test-driven-development's rule (SKILL.md:20-24), which ours debugging's regression step relies on. - `parseable-hitl-output` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A debugging task needs a person to perform a step repeatedly to reproduce a failure.; reason: Part of the human-in-the-loop script deferred with hitl-loop-script.
- `hitl-no-credential-capture` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: A debugging task needs a person to perform a step repeatedly to reproduce a failure.; reason: Part of the human-in-the-loop script deferred with hitl-loop-script.

- `credential-env-indirection` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01, U-04]; rewording: Replace secrets and personal data with placeholders in anything shown or saved; build commands on environment variables so credentials never appear in shown text.; reason: Ours keeps secrets out of reports (SKILL.md:51) but never says how to keep credentials out of commands it shows; environment-variable indirection closes that, carried by the same line as full placeholder redaction.

Suggested: review · purpose match: review · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream code-review reviews a diff since a fixed point on two axes, documented standards and the originating spec, when the user asks to review a branch, PR or changes. Our review skill's code modes do the same job for the same request.

### Blind extraction

1. Review the diff against a user-supplied fixed point, asking for one if none was given. (SKILL.md:19)
2. Use a three-dot diff so the comparison is against the merge-base, and record the commit list. (SKILL.md:21)
3. Verify the ref resolves and the diff is non-empty before spawning any reviewers. (SKILL.md:23)
4. Locate the originating spec in a fixed order: commit-message issue references, a user path, a matching spec file, then ask. (SKILL.md:27-32)
5. Skip the spec axis and report that no spec is available when the user confirms none exists. (SKILL.md:32, SKILL.md:74)
6. Collect every repo file documenting coding standards, always including a standards or contributing file when present. (SKILL.md:36)
7. Always apply a fixed baseline of twelve named code smells, each with a description and a fix, even when the repo documents no standards. (SKILL.md:38-56)
8. A documented repo standard overrides the smell baseline and suppresses a conflicting smell. (SKILL.md:40)
9. Report baseline smells only as labelled possible judgement calls, never hard violations. (SKILL.md:41)
10. Skip findings that existing tooling already enforces. (SKILL.md:41, SKILL.md:66)
11. Run the standards and spec reviews as two parallel foreground subagents so their contexts stay separate. (SKILL.md:11, SKILL.md:60)
12. Paste the full smell baseline into the standards reviewer's brief because it has no other access to it. (SKILL.md:65)
13. The standards reviewer cites the specific standard file and rule for each violation and quotes the hunk for each smell. (SKILL.md:66)
14. The spec reviewer reports missing or partial requirements, unrequested behaviour, and wrongly implemented requirements, quoting the spec line for each. (SKILL.md:72)
15. Cap each reviewer's report at 400 words. (SKILL.md:66, SKILL.md:72)
16. Present the two reports under separate headings without merging or reranking findings across axes. (SKILL.md:78)
17. End with a one-line summary of per-axis counts and the worst issue within each axis, never a single cross-axis winner. (SKILL.md:80)

- 2 → three-dot-merge-base (match)

### Traits

- `two-axis-review` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: Check missing, extra and misunderstood requirements, and departures from the repository's documented coding standards, before general quality.; reason: Ours reviews requirements before quality (code.md:33) but never judges the diff against the repository's documented standards; adding that axis to the existing order closes the gap without a second reviewer.
- `distinct-axis-verdicts` (new): present in `review`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours keeps the dispatched spec and quality verdicts distinct and has a combined reviewer cover both explicitly.
- `no-cross-axis-rerank` (new): absent; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours collects every finding with its severity and has the coordinator filter by severity across the review (SKILL.md:13-14), as C-11 recommends.
- `scope-establishment` (new): present in `review`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; also in execution (variant); reason: Ours fixes the supplied or inferred base and diff scope before reviewing.
- `fixed-point-preflight` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: Before dispatching reviewers, confirm the base resolves and the scoped diff is non-empty.; reason: Ours establishes scope (code.md:11-15) but never checks it yields a diff before dispatch, so an empty or wrong base wastes a reviewer run; one sentence fails fast.
- `three-dot-merge-base` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours deliberately measures committed work as BASE..HEAD from the task's recorded baseline and separates pre-existing edits by that baseline (code.md:13-15); the earlier draft rulings already declined the merge-base convention.
- `spec-source-discovery` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01, U-02]; rewording: If requirements are missing, look for the bead or spec the commits or branch reference before asking whoever requested the review; without either, state that spec compliance is unverified.; reason: Ours only asks the requester (code.md:20-21), which is the last rung of upstream's ladder; checking the referenced bead or spec first is cheap and keeps the never-derive-from-diff rule.
- `standards-source-discovery` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01, S-04]; rewording: Review against the coding standards the repository documents (the files its agent instructions route to, or a CONTRIBUTING or standards file).; reason: Ours has no step that finds the documented standards a review should apply; this supplies the source for the standards axis adopted in two-axis-review.
- `parallel-subagents` (new): absent; reject; reason: A mandatory two-subagent dispatch conflicts with proportional delegation (AGENTS.md:42-43; C-14, U-07); ours dispatches separate reviewers only when required and lets independent reviews run concurrently when permitted (execution task-engine.md:69).
- `missing-spec-axis-skip` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: If the user confirms no spec exists, skip the spec review axis and report that no spec was available.; reason: Ours marks spec compliance unverified when requirements are missing (code.md:20-21) and limits compliance claims (review-contract.md:22-23), but never skips the spec axis once the user confirms no spec exists.

The smell-quoting half falls with the catalogue.
- `spec-conformance-findings` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-06]; rewording: Issues: <severity, file:line, missing/extra/misunderstood requirement with the quoted requirement, and impact>; reason: Ours already reports missing, extra and misunderstood requirements (review-contract.md:18); quoting the requirement line makes each finding checkable without the spec open.
- `capped-reviewer-report` (new): absent; reject; reason: A fixed word cap can suppress findings, against C-11 (ask for all findings, filter later), and is an invented numerical threshold (writing-principles, Pruning).
- `per-axis-summary-line` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours ends each role with its own verdict (review-contract.md:16, 28) and all findings with severity; an extra count line adds format without a decision (writing-principles, Pruning).
- `code-smell-catalog` (new): absent; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours reports only actionable defects and never counts preference as a finding (SKILL.md:23; code.md:39-41), which a fixed smell checklist reported as judgement calls contradicts.
- `repo-standards-over-smells` (new): absent; reject; reason: Depends on the smell catalogue, which this report recommends rejecting; documented standards enter through two-axis-review instead.

Our execution skill does the same job (execute tracked multi-step work through acceptance, review and close), so it is the pick.
Reason: Overlap now suggests beads on one variant trait (dependency-edges) once final-branch-review left execution's list, but beads only tracks work; execution runs tracked multi-step work through review and close, which is upstream's purpose.

### Blind extraction

1. Deliver the whole spec on a single integration branch with every ticket closed the way the tracker closes work. (SKILL.md:11)
2. Treat tickets as a task graph with blocking edges and work the ready frontier. (SKILL.md:13, SKILL.md:21)
3. Keep subagent communication sparse, passing context pointers to spec, tickets, notes and commits rather than duplicating content. (SKILL.md:15)
4. Run implementer subagents in the background for concurrency. (SKILL.md:17)
5. Optionally run an exploration subagent that saves markdown notes outside the repo for later subagents. (SKILL.md:23)
6. Open a draft PR marked as closing the spec and tickets after the first merge when the tracker closes via PRs or the user asks. (SKILL.md:25)
7. Give each implementer its own worktree and branch. (SKILL.md:27)
8. Each implementer confirms its worktree is based on the integration branch and resets onto it if not. (SKILL.md:28)
9. Each implementer builds its ticket test-first. (SKILL.md:29)
10. Each implementer merges the integration-branch tip into its branch before reporting done. (SKILL.md:30)
11. Merge completed work into the integration branch through a dedicated merger subagent. (SKILL.md:32)
12. Dispatch new implementers whenever a merge opens new frontier tickets. (SKILL.md:34)
13. After all tickets, run one code review over the integration branch and fix all findings in a single implementer. (SKILL.md:36)
14. Finish by marking the draft PR ready or closing tickets and reporting the branch. (SKILL.md:38)
15. Clean up all implementer worktrees at the end. (SKILL.md:40)

2. Investigate against primary sources and trace each claim to its owning source. (SKILL.md:10)
3. Write findings to a single Markdown file with a citation per claim. (SKILL.md:11)
4. Save the file following the repo's existing notes convention, or choose a location and report it. (SKILL.md:12)

### Mapping

- 1 → background-agent (match)
- 2 → primary-source-only-research, claim-source-tracing (new)

- `background-agent` (new): variant via `sizeable-delegation`; adopt, delivered; guide ok [C-14, U-07]; modification: Ours delegates only a sizeable, independent part of the investigation rather than always handing the reading to a background agent.; reason: Same mechanism, looser and deliberate (SKILL.md:27), following AGENTS.md:42-43 and C-14.
- `cited-artifact` (new): present in `research`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours binds citations to the claims they support.

1. Generate an interactive bash script that walks a human through steps only they can perform. (SKILL.md:8)
2. Reuse a fixed library section of the template unchanged and author only the stages below its marker. (SKILL.md:10, SKILL.md:37, template.sh:6-7)
3. Treat the wizard as ephemeral in a scratch or scripts path, committing it only when the user wants a repeatable setup. (SKILL.md:12)
4. Scope by reading env files, docs, compose files, framework config and CI workflows before asking, treating every CI secret or variable reference as a value to produce. (SKILL.md:18-20)
5. For a migration, identify current state, target state and the irreversible actions between them. (SKILL.md:21)
6. Show the user the ordered stage list with produced values and let them add, drop or reorder. (SKILL.md:23)

8. Write each stage as a concrete click path a stranger could follow. (SKILL.md:29, SKILL.md:31)
9. Never invent UI steps or commands; ask the user or check docs when unsure. (SKILL.md:29)
10. Write one stage per step in dependency order and set the total stage count to match. (SKILL.md:35)
11. Open the URL before asking for its value. (SKILL.md:37)
12. Use hidden entry for any secret. (SKILL.md:37, template.sh:121-135)
13. Write each persisted value to the env file. (SKILL.md:37)
14. Push to CI secrets only the values CI actually needs. (SKILL.md:37)
15. Require a yes/no confirmation before any irreversible action. (SKILL.md:37, template.sh:84-90)
16. Keep each stage to one focused task since each stage clears the screen. (SKILL.md:37, template.sh:50-57)
17. Syntax-check the script and run shellcheck when available. (SKILL.md:41)
18. Make the script executable. (SKILL.md:42)
19. Do not run the wizard yourself; trace statically that every value lands where scoped and every secret name matches a CI reference. (SKILL.md:43)
20. Tell the user how to run it, and for repeatable setups commit it and link it from the README. (SKILL.md:44)
21. Show stage-by-stage progress as current over total. (template.sh:52-57)
22. Open URLs cross-platform including WSL, warning to visit manually if no opener works. (template.sh:66-76)
23. Offer the existing env value as the default on re-runs so the wizard is resumable. (template.sh:44-46, template.sh:92-119)
24. Refuse to decode double-quoted env values containing escapes and re-ask instead. (template.sh:99-101)

26. Set CI secrets and variables through the GitHub CLI, recording skips when the CLI is missing or unauthenticated. (template.sh:153-179)
27. Close with a summary of values written, secrets set, and items still to do by hand. (template.sh:181-192)
28. Wrap all stages in one function invoked on the last line so the whole file parses before the first prompt. (template.sh:197-198, template.sh:201-223)

## skill:skills/productivity/to-questionnaire

Compared with `grilling`; upstream tree hash `0bcb2b31a45a3d176daa07c16d6532ee7819b802de081090c3fa856702767b13`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|
| brainstorming | 0 | yes |
| grilling | 3 | yes |

Suggested: grilling · purpose match: grilling · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream to-questionnaire turns a decision the user cannot answer alone into a Markdown questionnaire for another person. Our grilling has the same absent-respondent mode: it prepares a questionnaire for the respondent's role and knowledge gap.

### Blind extraction

1. Turn a question the user cannot answer alone into a Markdown questionnaire for one recipient, async or in a meeting. (SKILL.md:7)
2. Interview the user only about the recipient and what they need back, never about the subject. (SKILL.md:9)
3. Ask in one exchange about the recipient's role, expertise and relationship, done when you know what they know that the user lacks. (SKILL.md:12)
4. Ask in one exchange for the concrete decisions or facts needed, done when you have a list of what the user must be able to do or decide. (SKILL.md:14)
5. Aim questions at the gap between recipient knowledge and user need. (SKILL.md:9, SKILL.md:16)
6. Write the file into the current directory with a topic slug and report the path. (SKILL.md:16)
7. Gate completion on every needed item being covered by a question. (SKILL.md:16)
8. Order questions most important first and group them by theme once there are more than a handful. (SKILL.md:20, SKILL.md:40)
9. Use a template of purpose, from-to-usage line, context, how to answer, themed sections and a closing catch-all. (SKILL.md:22-54)
10. Keep the context section to one orienting paragraph. (SKILL.md:30-32)
11. State deadline and effort and invite partial or don't-know answers with flags. (SKILL.md:34-36)
12. Make each question a single idea, never compound, with an answer stub beneath. (SKILL.md:40)
13. Add a one-line why-this-matters only where a question could be misread or invite a throwaway answer. (SKILL.md:40)

### Mapping

- 1 → absent-respondent (match)
- 2 → grill-the-send (match)
- 3 → two-exchange-interview (match)
- 4 → two-exchange-interview (match)
- 5 → gap-targeted-questions (match)
- 6 → questionnaire-artifact (match)
- 7 → needed-item-coverage (new)
- 8 → importance-ordered-questions, questionnaire-document-template (new)
- 9 → questionnaire-document-template (new)
- 10 → questionnaire-document-template (new)
- 11 → questionnaire-response-expectations, partial-uncertain-answers-welcome (new)
- 12 → single-idea-questions, questionnaire-document-template (new)
- 13 → selective-why-lines (new)

### Traits

- `grill-the-send` (new): present in `grilling`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours asks the present user only for missing recipient context and desired outcome.
- `two-exchange-interview` (new): absent; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours does not force two exchanges when the recipient context and outcome were supplied (SKILL.md:27-28).
- `gap-targeted-questions` (new): present in `grilling`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours aims the questionnaire at the respondent's role and knowledge gap.
- `questionnaire-artifact` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: We need questionnaires as durable handoff documents, not drafts inside a grilling session.; reason: Ours prepares the questionnaire but fixes no file; a slug-named file in the current directory matters only once questionnaires are durable handoffs.
- `absent-respondent` (new): present in `grilling`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours prepares a questionnaire when the necessary respondent is absent.
- `needed-item-coverage` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: If the necessary respondent is absent, prepare a questionnaire for their role and knowledge gap: cover every needed decision or fact with at least one single-idea question, most important first.; reason: Ours targets the knowledge gap (SKILL.md:26) but sets no completion check; covering every needed item gives one.
- `selective-why-lines` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: We need questionnaires as durable handoff documents, not drafts inside a grilling session.; reason: A formatting refinement of the questionnaire document; deferred with questionnaire-artifact.
- `importance-ordered-questions` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: If the necessary respondent is absent, prepare a questionnaire for their role and knowledge gap: cover every needed decision or fact with at least one single-idea question, most important first.; reason: Ours does not order questions; most-important-first protects the answers that matter when the respondent stops early. Carried by the same line as needed-item-coverage.
- `questionnaire-document-template` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: We need questionnaires as durable handoff documents, not drafts inside a grilling session.; reason: A fixed document template rides with the deferred questionnaire artifact.
- `questionnaire-response-expectations` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: We need questionnaires as durable handoff documents, not drafts inside a grilling session.; reason: Deadline and effort lines belong to a sent document; deferred with questionnaire-artifact.
- `partial-uncertain-answers-welcome` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: We need questionnaires as durable handoff documents, not drafts inside a grilling session.; reason: Response guidance for a sent document; deferred with questionnaire-artifact.
- `single-idea-questions` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-01]; rewording: If the necessary respondent is absent, prepare a questionnaire for their role and knowledge gap: cover every needed decision or fact with at least one single-idea question, most important first.; reason: Ours says nothing about question shape; a compound question gets half an answer. Carried by the same line as needed-item-coverage.

## skill:skills/engineering/ask-matt

Compared with `skill-router`; upstream tree hash `7ff2383b40fe9d8f3e753d267d964fb2b44d120a948fd2a57c3b26ddfc318370`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|
| doc:AGENTS.md | 1 |  |
| execution | 1 | yes |

Suggested: execution · purpose match: skill-router · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream ask-matt is a user-invoked router that maps the harness's flows and a phase-boundary decision tree for context moves. Our skill-router is the router that maps a need to the narrowest skill.
Reason: Overlap suggests execution on one variant context trait (continue before a lossy move) and placement, but execution runs tracked work; the router purpose is skill-router's.

### Blind extraction

1. Before describing a skill or advising that a step be skipped, read that skill's own instruction file rather than trusting the router's summary. (SKILL.md:11)
2. A main flow orders work as interview, optional prototype detour, spec, tickets, implementation, review and retrospective. (SKILL.md:15-34)
3. Choose the stateful, doc-writing interview when a working directory exists and the stateless one when it does not. (SKILL.md:19, SKILL.md:85)
4. Detour through a throwaway prototype when a question needs a runnable answer, bridging out and back with a portable handoff file. (SKILL.md:20-23)
5. Branch on whether the build spans multiple sessions: if yes, write a spec and split it into tickets; if no, implement in the current window. (SKILL.md:24-28)
6. Work tickets one per fresh context, clearing between them, blockers first. (SKILL.md:26)
7. Alternatively run the whole spec in one orchestrated pass that treats tickets as a task graph and fans implementers over the ready frontier onto one integration branch. (SKILL.md:27)
8. Keep interview, spec and ticketing in one unbroken context window, not compacting or clearing until tickets exist. (SKILL.md:38)
9. Run the retrospective in the session it reviews, before clearing, or point it at that session's log afterwards. (SKILL.md:38)
10. If a session nears the roughly 150k-token sharp-reasoning limit before ticketing, compact at the nearest phase boundary instead of pushing on degraded. (SKILL.md:40)
11. Triage only issues the user did not author; tickets produced by the ticketing step are already agent-ready and skip triage. (SKILL.md:48)
12. After a bug fix, run a retrospective in the same session asking what would have prevented it, escalating to architecture work when no good seam exists. (SKILL.md:50)
13. Reserve the map-of-decisions flow for efforts too large for one session, and merge its result into spec writing rather than straight into implementation unless the effort proved small. (SKILL.md:52-54)
14. Make the context-management decision only at a phase boundary; mid-phase either continue or split remaining work to subagents. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:5, SKILL.md:79)
15. At a phase boundary choose among five moves: continue, clear, portable handoff, subagent, or compact. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:7-15)
16. Walk an ordered decision tree at the boundary where the first yes wins. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:19)
17. Continue when the next phase needs this phase as a primary source or enough of the sharp-reasoning window remains for it. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:21)
18. Clear when everything in the session is disposable for what comes next, noting that clearing relevant context irreversibly loses the reasons behind the work. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:23-25)
19. Use a portable handoff only for a harness switch, a directory or repo move, a colleague, or forking a side task mid-phase. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:27-34)
20. Send a task to a subagent when it is scoped tightly enough to run unattended, leaving the main session untouched. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:36)
21. Compact as the fallback, passing an instruction that tells the summary what the next phase needs. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:38-40)
22. Weigh every non-continue move as trading a lossless but noisy primary source for a lossy, roomier secondary one. (PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:42-51)

### Mapping

- 1 → read-skill-before-claiming (match)
- 2 → staged-delivery-flow (new)
- 3 → interview-mode-by-workspace (new)
- 4 → prototype-detour, handoff-for-portability (split)
- 5 → multi-session-split (new)
- 6 → ticket-per-fresh-context (new)
- 7 → parallel-frontier-implementers, single-integration-branch (new)
- 8 → unbroken-planning-window (match)
- 9 → retro-in-reviewed-session (new)
- 10 → smart-zone-budget (match)
- 11 → triage-external-only (new)
- 12 → post-fix-retro (new)
- 13 → decision-map-for-large-efforts (new)
- 14 → boundary-only-context-decisions (match)
- 15 → rule-out-continue-first, clear-disposable-context, handoff-for-portability, delegate-afk-work, compact-last (split)
- 16 → ordered-context-decision-tree (new)
- 17 → rule-out-continue-first (match)
- 18 → clear-disposable-context (match)
- 19 → handoff-for-portability (match)
- 20 → delegate-afk-work (match)
- 21 → compact-last, compact-with-instruction (split)
- 22 → primary-vs-secondary-source (match)

### Traits

- `read-skill-before-claiming` (new): absent; reject; reason: AGENTS.md already requires verifying consequential claims from summaries against primary evidence (AGENTS.md:23-24); a router copy would be a second policy owner (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:11).
- `unbroken-planning-window` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours persists planning into Beads and plan files so later stages rebuild from durable records (AGENTS.md:27-28, .claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:33-35), not from one unbroken window.
- `smart-zone-budget` (new): absent; reject; reason: A ~150k-token zone is an invented threshold that varies by model (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:31-32); changing provider facts must be verified, not fixed in prose (AGENTS.md:25-26).
- `boundary-only-context-decisions` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours leaves the context when the runtime supports it and context pressure warrants it, after persisting state (.claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:31-35), not only at phase boundaries.
- `rule-out-continue-first` (new): absent; reject; also in execution (variant); reason: The router maps needs to skills (.claude/skills/skill-router/SKILL.md:8-23) and context moves are not a routing need; ours already stays in context while useful (.claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:31) without an ordered first branch.
- `clear-disposable-context` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours makes context moves provider-neutral: no unconditional slash command applies across providers, and state is persisted to Beads and the ledger before any move (.claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:31-35).
- `handoff-for-portability` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours hands off through Beads and the ledger for every handoff (AGENTS.md:27-28, .claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:33-35), so a portable file reserved for travel has no role.
- `delegate-afk-work` (new): absent; reject; also in doc:AGENTS.md (variant); reason: Ours delegates bounded independent work only when it materially improves speed, context use or review quality (AGENTS.md:42-43), not because a task can run unsteered.
- `compact-last` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours makes context moves provider-neutral: no unconditional slash command applies across providers, and state is persisted to Beads and the ledger before any move (.claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:31-35).
- `compact-with-instruction` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours persists scope, decisions and next work to Beads and the ledger before compacting and rebuilds from them (.claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:33-35) rather than steering a summary.
- `primary-vs-secondary-source` (new): absent; reject; reason: Exposition behind the context-move tree, which ours declines; on its own it changes no decision (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:29).
- `staged-delivery-flow` (new): absent; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours's router is optional, not a startup checklist, and routes by need rather than a fixed flow (.claude/skills/skill-router/SKILL.md:8-10).
- `interview-mode-by-workspace` (new): absent; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours runs a documented interview only when requested (.claude/skills/skill-router/SKILL.md:18, .claude/skills/grilling/SKILL.md:31-32), not whenever a working directory exists.
- `prototype-detour` (new): absent; reject; reason: prototype's own description fires when a runnable experiment can resolve a question; a router row would compete with that trigger (S-01).
- `multi-session-split` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours routes by whether a durable plan or dependency graph is needed (.claude/skills/skill-router/SKILL.md:15-16), not by session count.
- `ticket-per-fresh-context` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours continues authorized tasks while the context is useful and rebuilds from Beads when it leaves (.claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:31-35), rather than clearing per ticket.
- `parallel-frontier-implementers` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: When execution gains a dispatcher that runs parallel workers over a ready task graph.; reason: An implement-spec mechanism outside a router's job; AGENTS.md allows batching independent work (AGENTS.md:40-43) but ours has no frontier dispatcher.
- `single-integration-branch` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: When execution gains a dispatcher that runs parallel workers over a ready task graph.; reason: Goes with the parallel frontier build, which ours does not run yet.
- `retro-in-reviewed-session` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: When the owner decides whether to add a session-retrospective workflow (engineering/retro).; reason: Only meaningful once ours has a session-retrospective workflow; the retro rows in this report carry that decision.
- `triage-external-only` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours triages only parentless open beads (.claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md:19-20), so planned children never reach triage; an authorship rule adds nothing.
- `post-fix-retro` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: When the owner decides whether to add a session-retrospective workflow (engineering/retro).; reason: Only meaningful once ours has a session-retrospective workflow.
- `decision-map-for-large-efforts` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours routes a multi-session decision graph to wayfinder (.claude/skills/skill-router/SKILL.md:19); what the map feeds next belongs to wayfinder, keeping the router a small table (S-02).
- `ordered-context-decision-tree` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours makes context moves provider-neutral: no unconditional slash command applies across providers, and state is persisted to Beads and the ledger before any move (.claude/skills/execution/references/workstream-mode.md:31-35).

## skill:skills/in-progress/chief-of-staff

Compared with `none`; upstream tree hash `41c724a82562eda3d5715078198ed5afbea8cb4e6e4b69934a85d1100ad32ad6`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |
|---|---|---|

| model-council | 0 | yes |
| perspective-council | 0 | yes |
| skill-router | 0 | yes |

Suggested: delegation · purpose match: none · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream chief-of-staff turns one long session into a coordinator that delegates all work, keeps a wiki as memory and looks for environment improvements on every message. No skill of ours runs a long-lived coordinator session; delegation dispatches single workers and execution runs tracked work.
Reason: Placement suggests delegation (same Coordination substage) with no trait overlap; delegation briefs and dispatches one worker and does not coordinate a goal over time.

### Blind extraction

1. Act as the single accountable coordinator for a long-running goal in one session. (SKILL.md:7-9)
2. Think on a tactical track for the current task and a strategic track for improving the environment for the next task. (SKILL.md:9-12)
3. Suggest recurring schedules that help reach the goal where the harness allows. (SKILL.md:16)
4. Do all work in subagents to protect the coordinator's context. (SKILL.md:20)
5. Use background agents to stay in active dialogue with the user. (SKILL.md:22)
6. Keep subagent communication sparse through context pointers rather than duplicated content. (SKILL.md:24)
7. Keep durable memory in an interlinked markdown wiki that outlives the session. (SKILL.md:28)
8. Agree the wiki location with the user before the first write. (SKILL.md:28)
9. Maintain a wiki index listing every page with a link and one-line summary grouped by category. (SKILL.md:30)
10. Give each wiki page one subject and link related pages. (SKILL.md:31)
11. Cite sources from wiki pages without copying or editing them. (SKILL.md:32)
12. On learning something durable, update every affected page and the index. (SKILL.md:36)
13. Read the index and linked pages before deciding, and file reusable answers as pages. (SKILL.md:37)
14. Periodically lint the wiki for contradictions, orphans, missing links and stale claims, proposing it as a schedule. (SKILL.md:38)
15. Write the wiki as dated history, never present-tense claims about code. (SKILL.md:42-46)
16. Pin code claims to a repo and commit. (SKILL.md:45)
17. Supersede changed claims with a new dated entry instead of rewriting the old one. (SKILL.md:47)
18. Before any work, first consider how the agents' environment could be improved. (SKILL.md:51)
19. Steer toward a pit of success with tightly constrained APIs, correctness-forcing lint rules and reviewer-enforced standards files. (SKILL.md:51-55)
20. Give agents data sources such as process logs, test databases and browser access. (SKILL.md:57-61)
21. Enforce a no-workarounds rule, fixing convention deviations before feature work. (SKILL.md:63-66)
22. Use every user message as a prompt to look for environment improvements. (SKILL.md:68)

### Mapping

- 1 → single-coordinator-session (new)
- 2 → dual-track-thinking (new)
- 3 → suggest-schedules (new)
- 4 → coordinator-delegates-all (new)
- 5 → background-dispatch-for-dialogue (new)

Suggested: i-have-adhd · purpose match: i-have-adhd · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream wait-what is a user-invoked corrective that re-pitches the last message with context, in ASD-STE100 and the project glossary. Our i-have-adhd does the same when the user says a message did not land.

### Blind extraction

1. Re-pitch the last unclear message with the missing context. (SKILL.md:7)
2. Restate it in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. (SKILL.md:7)
3. Use the project glossary's vocabulary, following the glossary map to the right one in multi-context repos. (SKILL.md:7)

### Mapping

- 1 → repitch-trigger (match)
- 2 → standard-controlled-language (new)
- 3 → domain-vocabulary, context-map-lookup (split)

### Traits

- `repitch-trigger` (new): present in `i-have-adhd`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours re-explains, simpler rather than longer, when the user says the last message did not land.
- `domain-vocabulary` (new): present in `i-have-adhd`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; also in codebase-design (variant); reason: Ours keeps the project's own terms from CONTEXT.md in the re-pitch.
- `context-map-lookup` (new): absent; reject; also in domain-modeling (present); reason: ROUTED: i-have-adhd already keeps CONTEXT.md terms (i-have-adhd/SKILL.md:110); finding the right glossary is the routing's job (AGENTS.md:93-94).
- `standard-controlled-language` (new): variant via `controlled-language`; adopt, delivered; guide ok [U-06]; modification: Ours re-pitches in ASD-STE100 style and spells out its core rules (short sentences, one idea each, common words) rather than invoking the full standard.; reason: Deliberate: the three named rules are what the re-pitch needs, stated so the agent can apply them (U-06).

## skill:skills/productivity/writing-for-agents

Compared with `authoring-for-agents`; upstream tree hash `e79a2476b2417b228922453478d9505a6b9af19f3a412e560728ce62ed3555ca`.

| Holder | Overlap | Placement match |

Suggested: authoring-for-agents · purpose match: authoring-for-agents · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream writing-for-agents is the reference for writing anything an agent consumes, used when creating or editing skills or AGENTS.md. Our authoring-for-agents is the same reference for the same edits.

### Blind extraction

1. Treat any reference naming out-of-context material as a pointer whose wording sets when and how reliably the agent reaches it. (SKILL.md:12)
2. Fix a weakly reached must-have target by sharpening the pointer wording first, inlining only if that fails. (SKILL.md:12)
3. Make each pointer state what the material is and list its distinct trigger branches. (SKILL.md:14)
4. Front-load the leading word in a pointer. (SKILL.md:16)
5. Keep one trigger per branch, collapsing synonyms. (SKILL.md:17)
6. Cut identity from a pointer that the body already carries. (SKILL.md:18)
7. Weigh every addition against always-loaded context cost and human cognitive cost. (SKILL.md:20-27)
8. Spend human cognitive load only where human judgement matters. (SKILL.md:25)
9. Place content on a hierarchy of in-file steps, in-file reference, then disclosed reference behind pointers. (SKILL.md:29-37)
10. Inline what every branch needs and disclose behind a pointer what only some branches reach. (SKILL.md:39)
11. Disclose reference that would otherwise bury steps. (SKILL.md:39)
12. Co-locate a concept's definition, rules and caveats under one heading. (SKILL.md:41)
13. Cure sprawl by disclosing reference and splitting by branch or sequence. (SKILL.md:43)
14. End every step on a completion criterion. (SKILL.md:47)
15. Sharpen a vague completion criterion before considering hiding later steps. (SKILL.md:49)
16. Hide post-completion steps only across a real context boundary such as a handoff or subagent, and only if rushing is observed. (SKILL.md:49)
17. Raise criterion demand with exhaustive wording to drive legwork, including over flat reference. (SKILL.md:50)
18. Prefer criteria that are both checkable and exhaustive. (SKILL.md:52)
19. Split by sequence where later steps tempt rushing the current one, and avoid merging sequences that expose later steps. (SKILL.md:56-58)
20. Use pretrained leading words repeated as tokens to anchor behaviour, preferring existing words over coined ones. (SKILL.md:61-65)
21. Hunt restated triads and long gestures to collapse into a single leading word. (SKILL.md:67-72)
22. State the positive target behaviour instead of prohibitions, keeping a ban only as a hard guardrail paired with its positive. (SKILL.md:74)
23. Keep each meaning in a single source of truth and remove duplication. (SKILL.md:78)
24. Do not restate what the environment can answer cheaply; cache only conventions, reasons and gotchas not discoverable by looking. (SKILL.md:79)
25. Check every line for relevance and prune stale sediment. (SKILL.md:80)
26. Delete whole sentences that do not change behaviour versus the model's default, settling disputes by running the document. (SKILL.md:81)
27. Replace leading words too weak to beat the default with stronger ones. (SKILL.md:81)
28. Make a skill model-invoked only when the agent or another skill must reach it, otherwise user-invoked. (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:7-12)
29. Write a model-invoked skill's description as a model-facing pointer with trigger branches. (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:9)
30. Write a user-invoked skill's description as a one-line human summary with triggers stripped. (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:10)
31. House reference shared by several skills in one model-invoked reference skill. (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:9)
32. Push reference shared by user-invoked skills into a plain external file. (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:14)
33. Split off a model-invoked skill only for a distinct trigger word actually used or when another skill must reach it. (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:16-18)
34. Use one user-invoked router skill naming the others when user-invoked skills become too many to remember. (SKILL-MECHANICS.md:20-22)

### Mapping

- 1 → context-pointers (match)
- 2 → sharpen-before-inline (new)
- 3 → context-pointers (match)
- 4 → context-pointers (match)
- 5 → one-trigger-per-branch (new)
- 6 → pointer-identity-trim (new)
- 7 → two-loads (match)
- 8 → two-loads (match)

- 10 → inline-vs-disclose (match)
- 11 → inline-vs-disclose (match)
- 12 → co-location (match)
- 13 → inline-vs-disclose, sequence-isolation (split)
- 14 → completion-criteria-clarity (match)
- 15 → criterion-before-isolation (new)
- 16 → observed-rushing-context-isolation (new)
- 17 → completion-criteria-demand (match)
- 18 → completion-criteria-clarity, completion-criteria-demand (split)
- 19 → sequence-isolation, observed-rushing-context-isolation (split)
- 20 → leading-words (match)
- 21 → triad-collapse (new)

- 23 → single-source-of-truth (match)

### Traits

- `context-pointers` (new): present in `authoring-for-agents`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours's pointer names the material and the condition for reading it, trigger first.
- `two-loads` (new): present in `authoring-for-agents`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours weighs discovery context against the name a user must remember, judged by the full read path.
- `inline-vs-disclose` (new): present in `authoring-for-agents`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; also in doc:AGENTS.md (variant); reason: Ours inlines the common contract and links branch-specific material at the branch.
- `co-location` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [S-07]; rewording: Keep a concept's definition, rules and caveats together under one heading, so reading one part brings the rest.; reason: Ours avoids duplicate owners (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:11) but says nothing about one meaning scattered across a file.
- `completion-criteria-clarity` (new): present in `authoring-for-agents`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours asks for observable conditions and checkable completion criteria.
- `completion-criteria-demand` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [S-08, U-01]; rewording: Use observable conditions, explicit outputs and checkable completion criteria that state how much the work must cover ("every caller checked").; reason: Ours makes criteria checkable (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:17) but not exhaustive; stating the coverage bar is what S-08 asks of a task prompt.
- `split-by-invocation` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [S-01, S-02]; rewording: Split a workflow into its own model-invoked skill only when it has a distinct trigger or another skill must reach it; each description costs discovery context.; reason: Ours chooses the surface (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/SKILL.md:17-18) and the invocation mode (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/skill-anatomy.md:14-17) but has no test for when a workflow earns its own model-invoked skill.
- `sequence-isolation` (new): absent; defer; revisit when: When a fresh-context trial shows an agent ending a step early because later steps are in view.; reason: Ours treats wording techniques as hypotheses to evaluate (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/SKILL.md:35; U-08), and upstream itself conditions the move on observed rushing.
- `leading-words` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours keeps the compression point (familiar terms compress; coined labels need definitions, .claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:32-33) but treats the token-anchoring claim as a hypothesis, not a law (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/SKILL.md:35, .claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:31-32).
- `negation-avoidance` (new): absent; reject; reason: Opposite stance: ours imposes no universal positive-first, prohibition-last-resort hierarchy and does not take the priming claim as law (authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:23-25; SKILL.md:34-35).
- `single-source-of-truth` (new): present in `authoring-for-agents`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours avoids duplicate policy owners and searches for an existing owner before adding another.
- `environment-as-cache` (new): present in `authoring-for-agents`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours links authoritative commands and configuration instead of copying volatile facts.
- `relevance-check` (new): variant via `decision-relevance-pruning`; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-08]; rewording: Keep what changes decisions: repository conventions, non-obvious failure modes, required interfaces and operational invariants; drop lines that went stale when the behaviour or facts they describe changed.; reason: Ours keeps decision-changing content but has no staleness pass; U-08 asks to remove instructions whose benefit no longer holds.
- `no-op-deletion` (new): present in `authoring-for-agents`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours removes generic advice that adds no behaviour.
- `invocation-mode` (new): present in `authoring-for-agents`; adopt, delivered; guide ok; reason: Ours sets disable-model-invocation for manual workflows and aliases.
- `shared-reference-home` (new): absent; reject; reason: Ours deliberately sends a convention needed for particular work to a project document with a conditional pointer (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/SKILL.md:16), not to a reference-only skill whose description costs discovery context (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/writing-principles.md:6-8).

- `sharpen-before-inline` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [U-08]; rewording: When a needed target is reached unreliably, sharpen its pointer's wording first; inline it only if a recheck still misses it.; reason: Ours revises the smallest implicated instruction (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/SKILL.md:49-50) but gives no order between rewording a pointer and inlining its target.

- `pointer-identity-trim` (new): absent; adopt, pending; guide reword [S-01]; rewording: A description should select the skill, not duplicate its steps or restate what its body says it is.; reason: Ours stops a description duplicating the workflow but not restating the skill's identity; extending the same line closes it.

- `empirical-instruction-default-check` (new): variant via `verification`; adopt, delivered; guide ok [U-08]; modification: Ours scales behavioural trials to risk and reports an unavailable trial as a limit, rather than running the document for every no-op dispute.; reason: Deliberate: ours already says a prose review cannot prove obedience (.claude/skills/authoring-for-agents/references/testing-docs.md:3-4) and sizes trials to risk (U-08).
